findings.english_quote: “Forgiveness” is clear, idiomatic English for the soteriological ‘release’ of sins; “remission” is a viable traditional alternative noted in footnotes.
findings.issue: The lexical metadata says that “remission” is documented in the footnotes, but none of the supplied footnotes presents that alternative. This inaccurately describes the reader-facing disclosure; it is not a defect in the main rendering “forgiveness.”
findings.suggested_revision: Remove “noted in footnotes” from the lexical rationale, or supply a footnote documenting “remission” as an alternative. Any proposed replacement should receive fresh review.

findings.issue: The simplified edition independently contains the same inaccurate disclosure: its lexical metadata says “remission” appears in the footnotes, but its supplied footnotes do not document that alternative. The main rendering “forgiveness” remains source-compatible.

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all eleven paragraphs of the selected working Greek. Their main texts preserve the repentance/forgiveness distinction, difficult assertions, obligations, salvation and forgiveness conditions, speaker roles, and both remarriage permissions. Reader-facing “servants” and contextual “repentance” accord with current policy. The substantive negation alternative is disclosed without replacing the selected positive reading. The witness notes are compatible with the supplied bounded project reports and distinguish editorial restoration from preserved text; this does not authenticate unseen editions or manuscripts. Both editions need a minor metadata correction concerning the claimed “remission” footnote.
